Maintenance Supervisor – Full-Time
Location: Welshpool, Western Australia 6106
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $100,000 – $130,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking an experienced and motivated Maintenance Supervisor to join our growing team on a full-time basis.

About the Role
As a Maintenance Supervisor, you will be responsible for supervising maintenance personnel and coordinating preventative, corrective, and shutdown maintenance activities across mining, industrial, and heavy engineering projects. You will ensure maintenance work is completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with company procedures, client requirements, and Australian Standards.
Key Responsibilities
•	Supervise and coordinate daily maintenance activities across workshop and site operations.
•	Plan, schedule, and oversee preventative, corrective, and breakdown maintenance on plant, equipment, and machinery.
•	Allocate work to maintenance personnel and monitor productivity and work quality.
•	Ensure maintenance work is completed safely, on time, and within budget.
•	Inspect equipment and maintenance work to ensure compliance with engineering specifications, quality standards, and safety requirements.
•	Liaise with project managers, engineers, clients, and other departments to coordinate maintenance schedules and project requirements.
•	Investigate equipment failures, identify root causes, and implement corrective actions to minimise downtime.
•	Monitor maintenance records, service schedules, work orders, and equipment history.
•	Coordinate procurement of spare parts, tools, and maintenance materials as required.
•	Mentor, train, and support maintenance personnel, apprentices, and contractors.
•	Ensure compliance with workplace health and safety policies, environmental requirements, and company procedures.
•	Prepare maintenance reports, performance metrics, and recommendations for continuous improvement.

Skills and Experience
•	Minimum 1-2 years of full-time experience in a Maintenance Supervisor or similar maintenance leadership role.
•	Strong knowledge of preventative and corrective maintenance practices for industrial or mining equipment.
•	Experience supervising tradespeople in mining, oil and gas, fabrication, heavy engineering, or industrial environments.
•	Ability to interpret engineering drawings, maintenance manuals, and technical documentation.
•	Strong leadership, organisational, and problem-solving skills.
•	Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities.
•	Proficiency in maintenance management systems and Microsoft Office applications.
•	Strong commitment to workplace safety, quality, and continuous improvement.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $100,000 – $130,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work on major mining, shutdown, and industrial projects.
•	Ongoing training and career development.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.

Working alongside experienced engineers, you will be involved in structural analysis, modelling, documentation, and multidisciplinary coordination from concept through to construction while ensuring compliance with Australian Standards and project requirements.               Benefits   Competitive salary package.  Work on diverse and technically challenging building projects.  Ongoing professional development and mentoring from experienced engineers. Working under senior guidance, the engineer supports project delivery by producing accurate, buildable solutions that meet client, code, and program requirements.      Perform structural analysis, modelling, and design for building structures, including post-tensioned concrete slabs.  Prepare accurate engineering calculations, drawings, specifications, and design documentation.  Develop practical, efficient, and buildable structural solutions.  Coordinate structural designs with architects, civil engineers, services engineers, and drafters.  Ensure designs comply with Australian Standards (AS/NZS), the National Construction Code (NCC), and relevant authority requirements.  Use structural engineering software such as  ETABS, SAP2000, Strand7, SpaceGass, and RAPT  to develop and validate engineering solutions.  Assist with tender and construction documentation and respond to Requests for Information (RFIs).  Participate in project coordination meetings and provide technical support during construction.  Identify design risks, resolve engineering issues, and escalate complex matters to senior engineers where required.  Deliver assigned work within project timeframes, budgets, and quality standards.    Qualification & experience  Qualifications & Experience   Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Civil or Structural Engineering from a recognised tertiary institution.  Approximately  1–2 years' experience  in structural engineering within the building industry.  Experience in structural analysis, design, and documentation for commercial, residential, or mixed-use projects.  Knowledge of Australian Standards (AS/NZS), National Construction Code (NCC), and relevant engineering regulations.  Experience or demonstrated interest in  post-tensioned concrete design .  Experience using structural analysis and modelling software such as  ETABS, SAP2000, Strand7, SpaceGass, or similar .  Excellent written and verbal communication skills.  Ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.   The Skills We Need   Strong structural engineering and analytical skills.  Knowledge of structural modelling and engineering software.  Sound understanding of structural design principles and Australian engineering standards.  Excellent problem-solving and critical thinking abilities.  Strong organisational and time management skills.  Effective communication and stakeholder engagement skills.  Ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.  High level of attention to detail and commitment to quality.  Initiative, accountability, and willingness to continuously develop technical expertise.  Ability to manage multiple priorities while meeting project deadlines. With offices across Australia, Northrop provides specialist services in structural, civil, geotechnical, sustainability, transport, and building services engineering for projects across the commercial, residential, education, health, industrial, government, and infrastructure sectors.  At Northrop, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We foster a collaborative, inclusive, and supportive workplace where innovation, technical excellence, and professional development are encouraged. Guided by our core values— We Care, We Develop, We Empower, and We Build Relationships —we are committed to creating positive outcomes for our clients, our communities, and our people. The Client 

Blaze Engineering and Sheetmetal Fabrication Pty Ltd is a metal fabrication and engineering business based in Tullamarine, VIC, specialising in sheet metal fabrication, welding, metal assembly, and engineered manufacturing solutions.  

They are seeking an experienced Welder (First Class) to join their team in Tullamarine, VIC. 

 

The Role 

The Welder (First Class) is responsible for fabricating, assembling, and repairing metal components and structures using a range of welding and fabrication techniques. 

This is a full-time position with an annual salary of $78,000 to $82,000 plus superannuation. 

 

The Responsibilities 

Select and prepare appropriate welding equipment, consumables, and materials for welding operations. 

Read and interpret technical drawings, blueprints, welding procedures, and specifications to determine welding requirements. 

Mark out and cut metal sections and components using metal-cutting machinery. 

Shape and bend metal sections and plates using machine tools. 

Set up and operate MIG welding equipment to weld, join, and repair metal components and structures. 

Position and secure workpieces to ensure accurate alignment and welding in accordance with specifications. 

Perform welding operations on various metal components while maintaining required quality and safety standards. 

Inspect completed welds to ensure compliance with specified dimensions, quality requirements, and welding standards. 

Repair defective welds and damaged metal components through grinding, gouging, and rewelding processes. 

Perform weld finishing activities, including grinding and dressing welds to achieve the required finish and appearance. 

Use measuring and testing instruments to verify weld quality, accuracy, and compliance with specifications. 

Carry out welding repairs and maintenance on metal structures, machinery, equipment, and related components. 

Clean and prepare metal surfaces before and after welding to ensure quality. 

Conduct routine maintenance and basic troubleshooting of welding equipment to ensure safe and efficient operation. 

Follow workplace health and safety procedures, welding safety requirements, and relevant industry regulations at all times. 

Work collaboratively with supervisors, engineers, inspectors, and other trades personnel to complete welding tasks efficiently. 

Maintain accurate records of welding activities, inspections, repairs, materials used, and work completed. 

 

The Requirements 

Certificate IV in Engineering or equivalent qualification 

Minimum 1.5 years’ experience as a Welder (First Class) or within metal fabrication environments 

Minimum 1.5 years’ experience performing MIG welding across structural steel and fabricated metal components 

Minimum 1.5 years’ experience interpreting engineering drawings, fabrication plans, and technical specifications 

At least 1.5 years’ experience operating fabrication machinery, welding equipment, and metalworking tools 

At least 1.5 years’ experience assembling, repairing, and finishing fabricated metal products to engineering standards 

Sound knowledge of a range of welding techniques, including TIG, flux-cored and manual metal arc welding, and their application in metal fabrication. 

Strong knowledge of welding procedures, fabrication methods, and metal finishing techniques 

Ability to identify welding defects, dimensional inconsistencies, and fabrication issues accurately 

Strong understanding of workplace safety procedures, fabrication compliance standards, and workshop operations 

Good communication skills and ability to work effectively within fabrication and engineering teams 

High attention to detail and commitment to precision workmanship

This role is responsible for fabricating, welding, and repairing metal components for agricultural machinery while ensuring high standards of workmanship, quality, precision, and workplace safety.

Job Description

• Fabricate and weld various components for agricultural machines.

• Follow engineering drawings and specifications precisely to ensure the accurate assembly of parts.

• Operate a range of welding equipment to join metal parts and structures effectively.

• Interpret complex engineering drawings and blueprints to determine the layout and assembly of fabricated parts.

• Ensure fabricated components meet dimensional tolerances and quality standards outlined in engineering drawings.

• Conduct welding repairs and modifications as required to rectify defects or improve fabricated components.

• Perform thorough quality inspections of fabricated parts to identify defects, imperfections, or irregularities.

• Adhere to workplace health and safety procedures and safe operating practices to minimise workplace hazards and risks.

• Collaborate closely with the engineering team to communicate fabrication challenges, technical issues, and design improvements.

• Provide valuable feedback and recommendations to support continuous improvement of fabrication processes and product quality.

Qualifications / Attributes

• Must hold a Certificate III in Engineering – Fabrication Trade (Welding) or another relevant Certificate III, or at least three (3) years of relevant work experience may substitute for the formal qualification.

• Must possess at least one (1) year of relevant work experience as a Welder (First Class), Fabrication Welder, or in a similar welding role.

• Demonstrated ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, and technical specifications.

• Proficient in operating welding equipment and fabrication tools safely and efficiently.

• Strong understanding of welding techniques, fabrication processes, and quality assurance standards.

• High attention to detail with the ability to produce accurate, high-quality fabrication work.

• Sound knowledge of workplace health and safety procedures within a manufacturing or fabrication environment.

• Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to identify defects and recommend practical solutions.

• Ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively within a team environment.

• Reliable, safety-conscious, and committed to maintaining high standards of workmanship and continuous improvement.

Salary Range

$75,000 – $90,000 per annum excluding superannuation.

result.description:
Job Title: Control Room Operator (Engineering Technologist ANZSCO 233914)
Company: Scidell Pty Ltd, an associated entity of Multicom Resources Pty Ltd
Location: St Elmo Site, Julia Creek QLD 4823, Australia
Employment Type: Permanent, Full-time

About the company:
Our client Scidell Pty Ltd is a newly formed scientific delivery alliancing company of Multicom Resources Pty Ltd. Scidell is dedicated to providing cost-effective solutions to Multicom Resources, its foundation alliance client, while also seeking opportunities to expand its services.

Multicom Resources is a Queensland-based exploration and minerals refining company focused on discovering and developing world-class mineral deposits. Among its key projects is the Saint Elmo Project, located in the Northwest Minerals Province of Queensland. This project is advancing the production of vanadium and high-purity alumina, essential resources for global technology manufacturers.

About the role:
As a Control Room Operator at Scidell, you will play a vital role in the operations of the Saint Elmo Mine's mineral processing plant. Reporting to the Plant Manager, this position involves monitoring and optimizing plant equipment using advanced HMI systems and automated controls. You’ll be instrumental in ensuring plant safety, efficiency, and compliance with production goals and regulatory standards.
This is a full-time role operating on a rotating roster.

Key Requirements:
-A minimum of 1 year of experience in a similar role, such as a Control Room Operator, or within a related field, such as mining or mineral processing.
-A demonstrated ability to quickly learn and apply knowledge about process plant operations.
-Proficiency in operating and troubleshooting HMI and automated control systems (e.g., DCS, SCADA).
-Strong problem-solving skills to assess process disturbances and implement corrective actions effectively.
-Attention to detail to monitor plant conditions and identify operational changes.
-A commitment to maintaining safety and compliance with health, safety, and environmental standards.

Key Responsibilities:
-Monitor and control plant equipment using modern HMI and automated systems to ensure efficient and safe operations.
-Detect and respond to changes in process conditions and troubleshoot equipment issues.
-Collaborate with field operators and maintenance personnel to resolve process disruptions.
-Coordinate plant start-ups, shutdowns, and emergency operations to minimize downtime.
-Review plant performance data to identify trends and implement process optimizations.
-Support continuous improvement initiatives and contribute to enhancing plant efficiency.
-Maintain compliance with safety protocols and assist in training new operators.

Why Join Us?
Scidell offers a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge mineral processing projects while working in a supportive and collaborative environment. Be part of a team that values innovation, safety, and excellence in delivering critical minerals to global markets.

How to Apply:
If you're ready to be part of a dynamic team at Scidell Pty Ltd, dedicated to innovation and excellence, we’d love to hear from you! Please submit your application, ensuring you highlight your relevant experience and qualifications.

Scidell Pty Ltd is an equal-opportunity employer, committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds. While we appreciate every application, please note that only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

result.description:
Grounded Construction Group is currently looking to recruit an experienced and qualified Road Roller Operator to join their team in Muchea WA.


The Road Roller Operator is responsible for the safe and efficient operation of road rollers to compact soil, gravel, asphalt and other construction materials for roads, hardstands, building platforms and civil infrastructure works. The role is responsible for achieving specified compaction standards while maintaining compliance with company, client and legislative requirements.

The successful candidate will need to undertake and possess:

-  Operate road rollers safely and efficiently to compact soil, gravel, crushed rock, asphalt and other construction materials. 
-  Achieve specified compaction standards for roads, hardstands, building pads, foundations and civil infrastructure. 
-  Compact fill layers in accordance with project specifications and engineering requirements. 
-  Perform rolling operations for pavement construction, roadworks, drainage and site preparation activities. 
-  Read and work from construction drawings, survey pegs, compaction specifications and supervisor instructions. 
-  Monitor rolling patterns and identify areas requiring additional compaction. 
-  Coordinate safely with graders, excavators, loaders and other mobile plant during earthworks operations. 
-  Conduct daily pre-start inspections and complete required plant inspection documentation. 
-  Monitor equipment performance and report faults or maintenance requirements promptly. 
-  Carry out routine servicing, lubrication and minor maintenance within competency limits. 
-  Participate in pre-start meetings, toolbox meetings and safety interactions. 
-  Operate safely around personnel, mobile plant, underground services and fixed infrastructure. 
-  Maintain compliance with Grounded, client and statutory safety requirements. 
-  Complete required plant logs, inspection records and production documentation accurately. 
-  Assist with site establishment and other construction activities where required. 
-  Maintain housekeeping standards around work areas and equipment. 
-  Contribute to achieving project production, quality and safety objectives. 

Skills and Abilities:
-  Relevant qualification equivalent to AQF Certificate II or Certificate III, or equivalent industry experience. 
-  Minimum one (1) year relevant experience operating road rollers. 
-  Current Driver’s Licence (HR – MC Role Dependant) 
-  Operating SOA 
-  Operating VOC (2 years validity)


Salary range is $75,000 - $85,000pa commensurate with experience.

Fulltime Position available

Applications open on 20th July 2026 and closes on 20th August 2026

If you are interested in this role APPLY now. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted
